proposals.before: He was moved to literary aide to Prince of Yiyang, wash for the crown prince, then to left western aide on the grand steward's staff.
proposals.after: He was moved to literary aide to the Prince of Yiyang, then to fore-runner of the crown prince, then to left western aide on the grand steward's staff.
proposals.reason: 太子洗馬 is the office xima; rendering it as wash for the crown prince is a calque that conceals the appointment.

proposals.before: He was transferred to literary aide to Prince of Yiyang, wash for the crown prince, and moved to left western aide to the grand steward.
proposals.after: He was transferred to literary aide to the Prince of Yiyang, fore-runner of the crown prince, and moved to left western aide to the grand steward.
proposals.reason: Same calque of 洗馬 as wash rather than the official title.

proposals.before: He went out as chief clerk on Prince of Yuzhang Zishang's pacification staff, was moved to attendant at leisure, then again became chief clerk on Prince of Xin'an Ziluan's northern central commandant staff and administrator of Southern Donghai, with charge of southern Xuzhou—both posts were the emperor's beloved sons.
proposals.after: He went out as chief clerk on Prince of Yuzhang Zishang's pacification staff, was moved to attendant at leisure, then again became chief clerk on Prince of Xin'an Ziluan's northern central commandant staff and administrator of Southern Donghai, with charge of southern Xuzhou—both feudatories were the emperor's beloved sons.
proposals.reason: 二蕃 refers to the two princely establishments, not to Sengqian's posts.

proposals.before: Tan Gui of Gaoping had left office as administrator of Yuannan; Sengqian made him acting aide on the eastern-strike staff.
proposals.after: Tan Gui of Gaoping had left office as administrator of Yuannan; Sengqian made him acting aide on the Pacify-the-North staff.
proposals.reason: 征北 names the Pacify-the-North command, not an eastern-strike staff.

proposals.before: Tan Gui of Gaoping had left office as administrator of Yuannan; Sengqian made him eastern-strike staff acting aide.
proposals.after: Tan Gui of Gaoping had left office as administrator of Yuannan; Sengqian made him Pacify-the-North staff acting aide.
proposals.reason: 征北 is Pacify-the-North, not eastern-strike.

proposals.before: Your paternal cousin by marriage was Princess of Jiangxia; my own paternal aunt held the same rank as Princess of Nanqiao;
proposals.after: Your paternal cousin of the same grandfather was Princess of Jiangxia; my own paternal aunt of the same grandfather was Princess of Nanqiao;
proposals.reason: 同堂姊 is a same-grandfather cousin, not a cousin by marriage.

proposals.before: Gui wrote again: "Long ago Xun Yu was a pillar of the Han; only under Emperor Wu of Jin was his great-grandson ennobled.
proposals.after: Gui wrote again: "Long ago Xun Yu was a pillar of the Han; only under Emperor Wu of Jin was his great-great-grandson ennobled.
proposals.reason: 玄孫 is the fourth-generation descendant, not great-grandson.

proposals.before: Yang Hu at the opening of Jin proposed the campaign against Wu; only at the end of the Xiankeng era was his merit rewarded, when his brother's son was enfeoffed.
proposals.after: Yang Hu during Jin Taishi proposed the campaign against Wu; only at the end of the Xianning era was his merit rewarded, when his brother's son was enfeoffed.
proposals.reason: 晉泰始中 is during Jin Taishi; 咸寧 is Xianning, not Xiankeng.

proposals.before: Uncle Yangzi at Jin Taishi raised the plan to attack Wu — only by the end of Xiankeng were favor and reward heaped, enfeoffing his brother's son.
proposals.after: Yang Shuzi at Jin Taishi raised the plan to attack Wu — only by the end of Xianning were favor and reward heaped, enfeoffing his brother's son.
proposals.reason: 羊叔子 is the courtesy name Yang Shuzi, not Uncle Yangzi; 咸寧 is Xianning.

proposals.before: Bian Hu perished for the state at the start of the Xiankang era; only at the end of Xingning were rites and rank restored to his descendants.
proposals.after: Bian Hu perished for the state at the start of the Xianhe era; only at the end of Xingning were rites and rank restored to his descendants.
proposals.reason: 咸和 is Xianhe, not Xiankang (咸康).

proposals.before: In the first year of Shengming he was made vice director of the ministry of state, then directorate of the palace and left vice director; in the second year he became director of the ministry of state.
proposals.after: In the first year of Shengming he was made vice director of the ministry of state, then secretariat director and left vice director; in the second year he became director of the ministry of state.
proposals.reason: 中書令 is the secretariat director, not a directorate of the palace.

proposals.before: In Daming, at once used palace-suspended bells to harmonize the "Shield" and "Scepter" — though beat counts match, I fear straying from the Ya form; future connoisseurs of music may ridicule our sage age.
proposals.after: In Daming, at once used palace-suspended bells to harmonize the "Shield" and "Flywhisk" — though beat counts match, I fear straying from the Ya form; future connoisseurs of music may ridicule our sage age.
proposals.reason: The title 拂 names the flywhisk dance, not a scepter; the idiomatic line already has Flywhisk.

proposals.before: What Sengqian found in the world but not in the bundles were pieces by Wu's Great Emperor, Emperor Jing, the Marquis of Guiming, Huan Xuan, Chancellor Wang Dao, Pacification Army Wang Qia, Secretariat Director Wang Min, Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Boyu, and Zhang Yi—twelve fascicles in all, which he submitted.
proposals.after: What Sengqian found in the world but not in the bundles were pieces by Wu's Great Emperor, Emperor Jing, the Marquis of Guiming, Huan Xuan, Chancellor Wang Dao, Leader of the Army Wang Qia, Secretariat Director Wang Min, Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Boyu, and Zhang Yi—twelve fascicles in all, which he submitted.
proposals.reason: 領軍 is Leader of the Army, not Pacification Army (撫軍).

proposals.before: Wang Pingnan Yi, uncle to the Right General, were reckoned the best before the river crossing.
proposals.after: Wang Pingnan Yi, uncle to the Right General, was reckoned the best before the river crossing.
proposals.reason: Chinese names one man, Wang Yi, as the Right General's uncle; English plural were wrongly splits the subject.

proposals.before: Wang Pingnan Yi, the Right General's uncle, were held the finest before the crossing south.
proposals.after: Wang Pingnan Yi, the Right General's uncle, was held the finest before the crossing south.
proposals.reason: Same singular-subject error as the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: Fan Ye and Xiao Sihua studied under Yang Xin together; later Ye turned rebel a little; having lost his former footing, only retained a little intent.
proposals.after: Fan Ye and Xiao Sihua studied under Yang Xin together; later Ye departed a little from the model; having lost his former footing, he only retained a little intent.
proposals.reason: 後小叛 is a calligraphic metaphor for leaving the teacher's manner, not political rebellion.

proposals.before: His ninth son Ji, styled Zixuan, was swift and restless by nature and loved letters; whenever he read the biography of Fan Peng he could not keep from sighing in wonder.
proposals.after: His ninth son Ji, styled Zixuan, was swift and restless by nature and loved letters; whenever he read the biography of Fan Pang he could not keep from sighing in wonder.
proposals.reason: 范滂 is Fan Pang, not Fan Peng.

proposals.before: His ninth son Ji, styled Zixuan, was quick and restless by nature, loved literature; reading the biography of Fan Peng, he never failed to sigh in admiration.
proposals.after: His ninth son Ji, styled Zixuan, was quick and restless by nature, loved literature; reading the biography of Fan Pang, he never failed to sigh in admiration.
proposals.reason: Same personal-name error: 滂 is Pang.

proposals.before: You open the Laozi scroll a foot or five through the head, do not know what Fu asserts, what Ping expounds, how Ma and Zheng differ, what the Pointers and Examples clarify—and at once flourish the fly-whisk and call yourself a disputation master: this is the most perilous course.
proposals.after: You open the Laozi scroll a foot or five through the head, do not know what Fusi asserts, what Pingshu expounds, how Ma and Zheng differ, what the Pointers and Examples clarify—and at once flourish the fly-whisk and call yourself a disputation master: this is the most perilous course.
proposals.reason: Literal English truncates 輔嗣 and 平叔 to Fu and Ping, obscuring the courtesy names used as personal references.

proposals.before: He was made literary aide to the Prince of Baling, crown prince groom, northern central staff aide, crown prince attendant within the palace, chief rectifier of his native commandery, attendant on the chariot and horse staff, secretariat gentleman, commandery rectifier, and gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
proposals.after: He was made literary aide to the Prince of Baling, crown prince groom, northern central staff aide, crown prince attendant within the palace, chief rectifier of his native commandery, attendant on the chariot and horse staff, secretariat gentleman, provincial rectifier, and gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
proposals.reason: 州治中 is a provincial (zhou) post, not a commandery rectifier; the idiomatic list conflates it with 本郡中正.

proposals.before: He was again made senior crown prince aide and held the colonelcy of the assisting army; he became regular attendant and held the long river colonelcy; before long he also served as attendant, was moved to director of the ministry of personnel, and shared charge of the great selection.
proposals.after: He was again made senior crown prince aide and held the colonelcy of the assisting army; he became regular attendant and held the Changshui colonelcy; before long he also served as attendant, was moved to director of the ministry of personnel, and shared charge of the great selection.
proposals.reason: 長水校尉 is the Changshui colonelcy, a proper office title, not a ‘long river’ colonelcy.

proposals.before: He was again made senior crown prince aide and held the colonelcy of the assisting army; he became regular attendant and held the colonelcy of the long river; soon he also served as attendant, was moved to director of the ministry of personnel, and shared charge of the great selection.
proposals.after: He was again made senior crown prince aide and held the colonelcy of the assisting army; he became regular attendant and held the Changshui colonelcy; soon he also served as attendant, was moved to director of the ministry of personnel, and shared charge of the great selection.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 長水 as ‘long river’ instead of the office name Changshui.

proposals.before: He was moved to minister of rites for the imperial clan, again held the chief rectifiercy, was moved to grand minister of ceremonies, was given added rank as regular attendant, and soon held tutor to the Prince of Shi'an.
proposals.after: He was moved to minister of rites for the imperial clan, again held the chief rectifiercy, was moved to grand minister of ceremonies, was given added rank as regular attendant, and soon held the tutorship of the Prince of Shi'an.
proposals.reason: ‘Held tutor to’ is ungrammatical for 領始安王師 (concurrent tutor to the Prince of Shi’an).

proposals.before: When the emperor visited Zhuangyan Monastery to hear the monk Dadao preach, the seating was too far away for him to hear Xu speak. Reluctant to move Xu, the emperor instead moved Sengda nearer to him.
proposals.after: When the emperor visited Zhuangyan Monastery to hear the monk Sengda preach, the seating was too far away for him to hear Xu speak. Reluctant to move Xu, the emperor instead moved Sengda nearer to him.
proposals.reason: 僧達道人 is the monk Sengda; 道人 means monk and is not the personal name Dadao.

proposals.before: When the imperial carriage visited Zhuangyan Monastery to hear the monk Dadao preach, the seats were far apart, and the emperor could not hear Xu speaking; the emperor found it difficult to move Xu, and so moved Sengda closer to him.
proposals.after: When the imperial carriage visited Zhuangyan Monastery to hear the monk Sengda preach, the seats were far apart, and the emperor could not hear Xu speaking; the emperor found it difficult to move Xu, and so moved Sengda closer to him.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 道人 as the name Dadao rather than ‘monk’ modifying 僧達.

proposals.before: Zhang Xu bore a concentrated purity and an unadorned air, a nobility that came of itself; belted officials in court dress were what the age looked to and the people watched.
proposals.after: Zhang Xu bore a concentrated purity and an unadorned air, a nobility that came of itself; as a belted official in court dress, he was what the court looked to and the people watched.
proposals.reason: The phrase continues the portrait of Zhang Xu himself as a gentry official in formal dress who drew court and popular regard, not a separate group of belted officials.

proposals.before: The encomium runs: Jianmu's elder lord—his meaning wide and high.
proposals.after: The encomium runs: the venerable Jianmu—his righteousness vast and wide.
proposals.reason: Jianmu is Wang Sengqian's posthumous name used as the subject; the following word is an epithet for that elder gentleman, not a genitive locating him as elder of a place called Jianmu.

proposals.before: The encomium says: the elder of Jianmu—his principle is vast.
proposals.after: The encomium says: the venerable Jianmu—his principle is vast.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names Wang Sengqian by posthumous title plus an elder-gentleman epithet; Jianmu is not a place of which he is the elder.

decisions.reason: 太子洗馬 is the crown-prince staff office xima, not a washing chore; the replacement names that appointment and keeps the rest of the sentence.
The same calque of 洗馬 as wash is wrong in the literal line; fore-runner of the crown prince matches the office title.
二蕃皆帝愛子也 refers to the two princely establishments just named, not to Sengqian's posts.
征北 is the Pacify-the-North command; eastern-strike would be 征東, which the Chinese does not have.
Literal 征北 is likewise Pacify-the-North, not eastern-strike.
同堂姊 is a paternal cousin sharing a grandfather, not a cousin by marriage; 同堂姑 is a paternal aunt of that line, and 爲南譙王妃 means she was princess-consort of Nanqiao, not merely of like rank.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尚書同堂姊爲江夏王妃，檀珪同堂姑爲南譙王妃

decisions.after: Gui wrote again: "Long ago Xun Gongda was a pillar of the Han; only under Emperor Wu of Jin was his great-great-grandson ennobled.
decisions.reason: 玄孫 is the fourth-generation descendant (great-great-grandson), so that correction is required; the proposed after still keeps Xun Yu, but the Chinese names 荀公達 (Gongda), not 荀彧.

decisions.reason: 晉泰始中 is during Jin Taishi, not the opening of Jin, and 咸寧 is Xianning, not Xiankeng.

decisions.reason: 羊叔子 is the courtesy name Yang Shuzi, not Uncle Yangzi, and 咸寧 is Xianning.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 羊叔子以晉泰始中建策伐吳，至咸寧末

decisions.reason: 咸和 is the Xianhe era; Xiankang renders 咸康, which belongs to a later sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 卞望之以咸和初殞身國難

decisions.reason: 中書令 is secretariat director, not a directorate of the palace.
《拂》 is the Flywhisk dance; scepter is a mistranslation of 拂.
領軍洽 is Leader of the Army Wang Qia; Pacification Army would be 撫軍, which is not in this list.
王平南廙、右軍叔 names one man, Wang Yi, as the Right General's uncle; plural were splits that subject.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王平南廙、右軍叔，過江之前以爲最

decisions.reason: The literal line has the same singular subject and needs was, not were.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王平南廙、右軍叔，過江之前以爲最

decisions.reason: 後小叛 is a calligraphic remark that Fan Ye left the teacher's manner a little, not that he turned political rebel; adding he also repairs the broken clause.
范滂 is Fan Pang; Peng is the wrong reading of 滂.
The literal line has the same personal-name error: 滂 is Pang.
輔嗣 and 平叔 are the courtesy names Fusi and Pingshu; truncating them to Fu and Ping hides the persons named.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 未知輔嗣何所道，平叔何所說

decisions.after: He was made literary aide to the Prince of Baling, crown prince groom, northern central staff aide, crown prince attendant within the palace, chief rectifier of his native commandery, attendant on the chariot and horse staff, secretariat gentleman, provincial administrative aide, and gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
decisions.reason: 州治中 is a provincial administrative post, not a second commandery rectifier, but it is also not 中正; provincial rectifier still misnames the office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 本郡中正，車騎從事中郎，中書郎，州治中，黃門郎

decisions.reason: 長水校尉 is the Changshui colonelcy, a fixed office name, not a long-river colonelcy.
The literal line likewise must keep Changshui as the office name for 長水校尉.
領始安王師 is concurrent tutorship of the Prince of Shi'an; held tutor to is ungrammatical, and the proposed tutorship wording is accurate.
僧達道人 is the monk Sengda; 道人 means monk and is not the name Dadao.
The literal line makes the same error: 道人 modifies 僧達 as monk, not a second personal name.
搢紳端委，朝宗民望 continues the portrait of Zhang Xu in formal dress as the person the court turned to and the people watched, not a separate class of officials as the grammatical subject.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 張緒凝衿素氣，自然標格，搢紳端委，朝宗民望

decisions.reason: 簡穆 is Sengqian's posthumous name and 長者 an epithet for that elder gentleman; Jianmu is not a place whose elder he is, and 義恢恢 is vast righteousness, not meaning.
The literal elder of Jianmu likewise treats the posthumous title as a place; venerable Jianmu restores the epithet.

claimRetractions.reason: s0072 names 荀公達 only; the personal name Xun Yu is an identification invented by the English and is the wrong man (Gongda is Xun You, not Xun Yu).
道人 in 僧達道人 means monk; it is not an alternate personal name Dadao.

claimRevisions.reason: 玄孫 is great-great-grandson, four generations down; the extracted English great-grandson follows the unrepaired translation.

value.en: Leader of the Army Wang Qia

claimRevisions.reason: The title attached to 洽 is 領軍, Leader of the Army, not Pacification Army.
范滂 is Fan Pang; Fan Peng is only the mistranslation.
州治中 is a provincial administrative aide, not a rectifier (中正); the extracted English still uses rectifier.
